text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyThe Secrets Hiding in a Duck-Billed Dinosaur’s BeakThey were more sophisticated than previously thoughtJCBy Jake Currie7:00 AM CST on November 21, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHadrosaurs might not be the most popular dinosaurs among children, but they were extremely popular with natural selection. These duck-billed dinosaurs were some of the most common types of herbivores living during the Cretaceous period, and as such, they’re well-represented in the fossil record. Remarkably, we’re still learning new things about them and their eponymous bills.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayFor more than a decade, paleontologists puzzled over a series of bony projections around the front rim of the upper jaw of Tethyshadros, a genus of duck-billed dinosaur first discovered in Italy’s Villaggio del Pescatore.
